$comment: Market Street Railway numbered lines (Phase 2c). Hand-kept; each route is written by transit_pipeline.street_routes from routes.json.

lines.name: No. 1 Sutter and California Streets
lines.summary: In 1909 the line started at Market and Sutter Sts; by 1929 it ran from the Ferry and went on out Clement St.

sources.note: "7/ 2/49 No. 1 — Last day of street car operation." Motor coaches from July 3, 1949.

lines.name: No. 3 Sutter and Jackson Streets
lines.summary: Out Sutter St, Fillmore St and Jackson St to Presidio Ave. Manley's report of 1909 says it "has just resumed service".

sources.note: "7/ 2/49 No. 3 — Last day of street car operation."

lines.name: No. 4 Turk and Eddy Streets
lines.summary: Out Eddy St and back on Turk St, then Divisadero St, Sacramento St and Lake St to a loop in the Richmond district (Manley spells it Devisadero).

sources.note: "7/31/48 No. 4 — Last day of street car operation."

route.note: Manley (1909) says "Sacramento to Lake", which meet only here
Back toward Lake St. Manley (1909): "to Fulton to 6th Ave. and return", the loop No. 24 ran the other way ("Lake to 6th to Fulton to 8th to Clement to 6th", p. 16)

lines.name: No. 6 Haight Street and Masonic Avenue
lines.summary: In 1909 the "Masonic" line ran out Hayes St, Fillmore St and Oak St (back on Page St), then by Masonic Ave, Frederick St, Clayton St, Carl St and Stanyan St "to Parnassas Ave. to Affiliated Colleges"; Manley calls the name "a misnomer, as it runs for but three blocks on Masonic Ave". By 1929 it ran out Haight St and on to 9th Ave and Pacheco St.
lines.fate_note: Motor coaches from July 4, 1948; trolley coaches from 1949.

sources.note: "7/ 3/48 No. 6 — Last day of street car operation."

route.note: Manley (1909): "to Stanyan to Parnassas Ave. to Affiliated Colleges", without the cross street where the cars stopped; drawn to Judah St, as in 1929

lines.name: No. 7 Haight Street and Ocean
lines.summary: Out Haight St to Stanyan St; by 1929 on by Frederick St and Lincoln Way, then a private right of way (not drawn: its course isn't given) to the beach at Balboa St.
lines.fate_note: Motor coaches from July 4, 1948; trolley coaches from July 3, 1949.

sources.note: "7/ 3/48 No. 7 — Last day of street car operation."

lines.name: No. 8 Market Street
lines.summary: Out Market St to Castro St and 18th St. Manley (p. 28) says the Castro St cable line acted "as an extension of the Market Street line No. 8, which stops at 18th and Castro".

sources.note: "7/ 1/49 No. 8 — Last day of street car operation."

lines.name: No. 9 Valencia Street
lines.summary: Out Market St, Valencia St and Mission St to 29th St and Noe St.

sources.note: "1/15/59 No. 9 — Last day of street car operation." Motor coaches from January 17, 1949. The year is misprinted: the entry stands among those of January 1949, in the report for 1948–49, on the same day as Nos. 11 and 14. The report prints its dates in a column apart from the entries; this one was read on the page image.

lines.name: No. 10 Guerrero Street and Sunnyside
lines.summary: Out Mission St, 14th St, Guerrero St and San Jose Ave; by 1929 on by 30th St, Chenery St, Diamond St and Monterey Blvd to Genessee St. In 1909 two lines were numbered 10, the Guerrero line ("to 14th Street to San Jose Avenue and Ocean View") and the Glen Park line ("to 14th to Guerrero to Chenery Street and San Jose Ave."), "over the same tracks most of the way" (Manley p. 20); where either ended in 1909 isn't given street by street, so in 1909 it is drawn to 30th St.

route.note: From the Ferry Building to Mission St
Manley (1909): the Guerrero line ran "to San Jose Avenue and Ocean View", and the Glen Park line "to Chenery Street and San Jose Ave."
30th St from San Jose Ave to Chenery St; the stretch of today's track drawn reaches Church St, a block on
To Genessee St, as the report spells it

lines.name: No. 11 Mission and 24th Streets
lines.summary: Out Mission St, 22nd St, Chattanooga St and 24th St to Hoffman Ave; by 1929 back by Dolores St.

sources.note: "1/15/49 No. 11 — Last day of street car operation." Motor coaches from January 17, 1949. The report prints its dates in a column apart from the entries; this one was read on the page image.

route.note: From the Ferry Building to Mission St

lines.name: No. 12 Mission Street and Ingleside
lines.summary: Out Mission St, Onondaga Ave and Ocean Ave; in 1909 "to Ocean Avenue to Ingleside" (drawn to San Jose Ave, since where the cars stopped isn't given), by 1929 on by Sloat Blvd to the Great Highway.

sources.note: "10/31/48 No. 12 — Last day of street car operation." The report prints its dates in a column apart from the entries; this one was read on the page image.

route.note: From the Ferry Building to Mission St
Manley (1909): "to Onondaga Avenue to Ocean Avenue to Ingleside"
O'Shaughnessy names Ocean Ave and Sloat Blvd; between them the map follows today's K line track by Junipero Serra Blvd to St Francis Circle

lines.name: No. 14 Mission Street and Daly City
lines.summary: Out Mission St to Daly City; in 1909 the "Cemeteries" line ran on through Colma to the cemeteries (its end isn't given).
lines.fate_note: Motor coaches from January 1949, with express service from Richland Ave and Mission St to Fifth St.

sources.note: "1/15/49 No. 14 — Last day of street car operation." Motor coaches from January 16, 1949. The report prints its dates in a column apart from the entries; this one was read on the page image.

route.note: From the Ferry Building to Mission St

lines.name: No. 15 Kearny Street and North Beach
lines.summary: From the Southern Pacific station at 3rd and Townsend Sts by 3rd St, Kearny St, Broadway and Powell St to North Beach: to Bay St in 1909, to Jefferson St by 1929.

lines.name: No. 17 Haight Street and Ingleside
lines.summary: Out Haight St, Frederick St, Lincoln Way, 20th Ave, Wawona St and 19th Ave to Sloat Blvd. There was no No. 17 in February 1909 (Manley p. 34).

sources.note: "12/23/45 No. 17— Discontinued." The last day isn't given.

lines.name: No. 18 Mission Street and Daly City
lines.summary: From Market St by 5th St and Mission St to Daly City. In 1909 No. 18 was the Polk and Mission line, on other streets (Manley p. 16).

lines.name: No. 19 Ninth and Polk Streets
lines.summary: From Brannan St by 9th St, Larkin St, Post St and Polk St to North Point St. In February 1909 No. 19 was the Bryant and Polk line; Manley adds that it had since been replaced by a Ninth and Polk line, "designated No. 19" (p. 16).

sources.note: "9/23/45 No. 19 — Street car service discontinued." Motor coaches on the No. 19 from the next day. The last day isn't given.

lines.name: No. 20 Fourth, Ellis and O'Farrell Streets
lines.summary: Out Ellis St, O'Farrell St, Divisadero St and Oak St to Stanyan St, back by Page St and Ellis St, and from Market St by 4th St to the Southern Pacific station. In 1909 the cars went on "to Stanyan to H to 19th", and every other car "out H to Ocean Boulevard, thence west to B Street" (Manley p. 18; not drawn yet: that H St is today's Lincoln Way isn't sourced here).

sources.note: "9/27/47 No. 20 — Last day of street car operation." Motor coaches from September 29, 1947. The report prints its dates in a column apart from the entries; this one was read on the page image.

lines.name: No. 21 Hayes Street
lines.summary: Out Hayes St to Stanyan St, and out Fulton St to 8th Ave. In 1909 the Hayes and Ellis line came out Ellis St and O'Farrell St (back by Ellis St) and turned into Hayes St at Divisadero St, and Fulton St from 8th Ave was its "extension" (Manley p. 29); by 1929 it ran from the Ferry out Market St and Hayes St, and on by 8th Ave to Clement St.
lines.fate_note: Motor coaches from June 7, 1948; trolley coaches from July 3, 1949.

sources.note: "6/ 7/48 No. 21 — Motor coach service substituted for street car service. Last day of street car operation June 5, 1948."

route.note: Manley (1909) gives the route "to Stanyan to Fulton", and Fulton St "from 8th Avenue" as "the extension of the Geary, Turk and Eddy, McAllister, and Hayes Street lines" (p. 29)
Manley (1909) gives the route "to Stanyan to Fulton", and Fulton St "from 8th Avenue" as "the extension of the Geary, Turk and Eddy, McAllister, and Hayes Street lines" (p. 29)

lines.name: No. 27 Bryant Street
lines.summary: From Market St by 2nd St and Bryant St to 26th St and Mission St, back by Brannan St. In 1909 the unnumbered Bryant line ran on the same streets, back by 10th St; by 1929 back by 8th St.

sources.note: "8/13/48 No. 27 M.C. — Last day of street car operation."

lines.name: No. 32 Hayes and Oak Streets
lines.summary: Weekdays until 5:47 p.m.: out Hayes St, Fillmore St and Oak St to Stanyan St, back by Page St. In 1909 the Masonic line (No. 6) ran on these streets.

lines.name: No. 33 Eighteenth Street and Park
lines.summary: From 3rd St by Harrison St, 14th St, Guerrero St and 18th St, over Market St and Caselli Ave to Clayton St, Ashbury St, Frederick St and Waller St to Stanyan St. In 1909 the unnumbered Eighteenth line ran much of this way (Manley p. 20), by a "Falcon Avenue" not yet placed.

route.note: To Caselli Ave, which meets Market St at Clayton St

lines.name: No. 34 Sixth and Sansome Streets
lines.summary: From Brannan St by 6th St, Taylor St, Post St, Kearny St, Bush St and Sansome St to Chestnut St. In 1909 it was the unnumbered Sixth and Sansome line, made "one continuous line" when its Post St track came into use (Manley p. 19).

lines.name: No. 36 Folsom Street
lines.summary: Out Folsom St to Precita Ave. Manley's unnumbered Folsom line (1909) ran "Out Folsom from the Ferry to 26th and Precita Avenue"; by 1929 it reached Folsom St by Howard St and Steuart St, and went on to York St. The map starts it at Spear St: Steuart St no longer reaches Folsom St, and the 1909 route from the Ferry isn't given street by street.

sources.note: "10/28/45 No. 36 — Line changed from street car to motor coach operation." The last day isn't given.

lines.name: No. 41 Second and Market Streets to the Southern Pacific depot
lines.summary: Weekday rush hours, timed to the Southern Pacific's peninsula trains: from Market St by 2nd St and Brannan St to the station at 3rd and Townsend Sts.

sources.note: "1/15/49 No. 41 — Discontinued. Service by "F" line." The last day isn't given. The report prints its dates in a column apart from the entries; this one was read on the page image.

lines.name: No. 42 First and Fifth Streets
lines.summary: A loop south of Market St: from California St by Battery St, 1st St, Folsom St, 2nd St, Brannan St, 3rd St, Townsend St, 4th St and Brannan St to 5th St and Market St, back by 5th St, Brannan St, 2nd St and Folsom St.

lines.name: Tenth and Post Streets
lines.summary: From Bryant St by 10th St, Polk St, Hayes St, Larkin St, McAllister St, Leavenworth St and Post St to Montgomery St and Market St. In 1909 the Montgomery and 10th line ran from 10th and Bryant Sts by City Hall to Montgomery St (Manley p. 19).

lines.name: Divisadero Street extension
lines.summary: A shuttle on Divisadero St between Sacramento St and Jackson St.

lines.name: No. 40 San Mateo

running.note: "The cars at the present time are operated every half-hour" to San Mateo.
"5th and Market via 5th to Mission to Colma to Cemeteries to San Mateo."

lines.summary: The San Mateo interurban: from 5th and Market out Mission St through Daly City and Colma, then on its own right of way by the cemeteries, San Bruno and Millbrae to Burlingame, and through the streets of San Mateo to Main St.
lines.fate_note: Abandoned on January 16, 1949, the last day of operation being January 15, 1949 (the San Francisco PUC's report for 1948-49).

sources.note: "Line No. 40 - San Mateo From Market St. via 5th St., Mission St., through Daly City and Colma, then Private Right of Way through San Bruno, Lomita Park and Millbrae to Burlingame, then via San Mateo Drive, Baldwin Avenue, "B" Street and 3rd Ave. to Main Street - San Mateo."
"On January 16, 1949, the No. 40 San Mateo street car line was abandoned, the last day of operation being January 15, 1949."

lines.notes: Its opening to San Mateo isn't sourced; the map draws it from October 31, 1903, when the Street Railway Journal describes the cars running (decision 20). In 1903 it reached the city by the San Francisco & San Mateo's streets of 1892, which aren't drawn yet, so until 1909 it is drawn from Daly City. Its streets in San Mateo are O'Shaughnessy's of 1929; the ones before aren't sourced.

route.note: Back by Main St, 2nd Ave, B St, Baldwin Ave, Ellsworth Ave and Poplar Ave
